kpis.sub: MP FLAT ON THE WEEK, BUT SHORT INTEREST CLIMBS TO 22.4% AS ANALYSTS TRIM TARGETS (OCT 9 CLOSE)
kpis.label: MP Materials closed $46.15 on Oct 9 (vs ~$46.96 on Oct 2), inside a $37.81–$100.25 52-week range on an $8.22B market cap. Short interest rose ~9% in a month to 22.40% of float (6.8 days to cover). Morgan Stanley cut its target from $73 to $66 (rating reported unchanged at overweight) and the stock fell ~4.8% intraday on Oct 7–8; consensus remains Moderate Buy at ~$75. REMX hit a new one-year low (~$60.97, about -17.5% YTD). Q3 results are expected around Nov 5 (estimated). MP also sits in the Robotics sleeve — don't double-count

kpis.sub: CHINA'S EXPORT-CONTROL SUSPENSION EXTENDED TWO MONTHS — THE NOV 10 CLIFF IS NO LONGER THE DATE
kpis.label: Treasury Secretary Bessent announced on Sep 23, as Xi arrived in Washington, that the US-China truce — including the suspension of Beijing's Oct 2025 rare-earth controls on products with 0.1% Chinese content — now runs to Jan 10, 2027. Markets had hoped for 6–12 months; only the date changed, with no new terms, and China's April 2025 licensing on seven elements was never suspended. Correction: earlier editions of this page still showed Nov 10 as the deadline. The White House says rare-earth shipments have not returned to agreed levels

kpis.sub: LITHIUM CARBONATE FUTURES FLAT NEAR $18.3K, WELL BELOW MAY'S PEAK (GFEX, OCT 11)
kpis.label: Guangzhou lithium carbonate futures tracked ~$18,290/t on Oct 11, effectively unchanged from a week earlier and down ~30% from the mid-May high above 200,000 yuan. Supply restarts (CATL's Jianxiawo, Australian producers) are stoking 2027 glut fears even as China battery output grows; a US DLA solicitation for ~16,000t of lithium carbonate (up to $300M) is a small policy offset. Albemarle closed $101.28 and Lithium Americas $2.35 (a fresh 52-week low)

kpis.sub: LME COPPER ~2% BELOW THE SEP 10 RECORD AS A CHILEAN STRIKE BEGINS (OCT 8)
kpis.label: Three-month LME copper rose ~1% to $14,614.5/t on Oct 8, about 2% under the $14,875 record set Sep 10, as Chinese buyers restocked after the National Day holiday. A legal strike began Oct 7 at Antofagasta's Centinela mine (709 workers, ~22% of its workforce; the mine made 240,400t in 2025); unions warn supply effects could show by November. Freeport closed $73.68 on Oct 9 (+3.6% on the day) versus a $76.22 consensus target and an $80.24 52-week high; Grasberg is still recovering

themes.title: The cliff moved to Jan 10, 2027 — and the scarcity premium kept deflating anyway
themes.description: The Trump–Xi summit bought only two more months: the suspension of China's Oct 2025 controls now lapses Jan 10, 2027 rather than Nov 10, with no new terms and the April 2025 seven-element licensing still in force. Rare-earth equities fell regardless — REMX made a new one-year low and MP's short interest reached 22.4% — which shows the market is pricing a thaw, not a structural fix. Western separation, metallization and magnet capacity is still thin, and America's DFARS magnet restrictions move to a new phase by the same January date.

themes.title: House Republicans assemble a four-bill package on mining permits and a federal stockpile
themes.description: As of Oct 6, a package led by the Critical Mineral Dominance Act (H.R. 4090, passed the House 224-195 and now awaiting Senate action) would speed mining on federal land, expand FAST-41 permitting, and create a Strategic Resilience Reserve (the Senate SECURE Minerals companion proposes $2.5B). Passage is uncertain — H.R. 4090 sits in the Senate Energy committee — but the NDAA is a possible vehicle. Policy support is broad, yet slow-moving relative to the market's patience.

themes.title: Demand-side backstops keep widening, but they favor projects that already exist
themes.description: Project Vault's VaultCo (Glencore and Mercuria committed $1B on Sep 23, on top of $10B of EXIM financing) and the Pentagon's NdPr, dysprosium and terbium floors insulate funded producers, while the Sep 22 US–Denmark–Greenland security agreement and Greenland Mines' Sarfartoq deal extend the supply map. None of this helps a developer without product to sell, and trader-led procurement does not automatically favor US producers.

rows.angle: Largest non-China rare-earth producer (Australia/Malaysia); pushing into heavy rare earths
rows.watch for: Amanda Lacaze left in late August after ~12 years and no permanent CEO has been named. FY26 REO output hit a record 13,089t, but NdPr was only 7,260t against 10,500t nameplate, so earnings stay sensitive to depressed NdPr prices. The ~A$294M heavy-rare-earth facility is progressing (samarium oxide started March 2026), and the Malaysian licence runs to 2036 with a condition to end radioactive waste generation by ~2031. (Lynas price/news not refreshed this week; no permanent CEO announcement found.)

rows.angle: Copper — the electrification metal at scale

bear_case.title: The premium keeps deflating faster than the supply chain is built
bear_case.description: Even with the truce extended to Jan 10, REMX hit a one-year low (~$60.97, -17.5% YTD), MP sits ~54% below its $100.25 high and short interest in MP (22.4%) and USAR (20.3%) is rising. MP is still loss-making at the EPS line on a ~20x P/S, and Western separation, metallization and magnet capacity remain thin. An eventual deal that rolls the truce again could compress the premium further before real capacity arrives.

bear_case.title: Commodity cycles cut both ways
bear_case.description: Lithium carbonate futures are flat near $18.3k/t, ~30% under May's peak, with supply restarts stoking 2027 glut fears; Albemarle ($101.28) and Lithium Americas ($2.35, new low) reflect it. Freeport is within ~3.5% of its consensus target with copper near record highs, so much good news is priced in. A producer can be an excellent business at the wrong point in its price cycle.

bear_case.title: China can flood, freeze or consolidate
bear_case.description: Beijing's controls are suspended, not repealed: they can return Jan 10, 2027, and the April 2025 seven-element licensing was never lifted. The White House says rare-earth shipments have not returned to agreed levels, so the leverage remains. A flood of cheap Chinese NdPr would undercut non-Chinese producers even with Pentagon floors, which only protect projects that already have product.

bear_case.title: Junior dilution, leadership gaps and policy dependency
bear_case.description: USAR, UUUU and LAC trade at or within a few percent of 52-week lows while funding multi-year builds, and equity raises are the standard way juniors fill the gap. Lynas has no permanent CEO and Albemarle's arrives in Feb 2027. The Vault, EXIM funding, DoD floors and the House package are real but discretionary, and H.R. 4090 still has to clear the Senate.
